candidates.subject: southern masked weaver
candidates.title: Held below
candidates.body:
The walls are finished, but I still land on the branch beside them. I know what a branch can hold. I had watched half the grass in this nest fall past me at least once.

Today I missed the branch. One foot caught the rim. The other followed, and I swung underneath the whole green thing.

It held.

I pulled myself toward the wood, then stopped. My feet were pulling at grass. The grass was pulling at more grass. Somewhere above me was the little join I'd nearly thrown away.

Let go with one foot. Put it back. Tried the other.

A loose end brushed my face. I reached to tear it out, remembered what I was hanging from, and tucked my bill shut.
candidates.visibleScene: Male southern masked weaver hangs beneath a woven green nest with legs raised toward its lower edge; a vertical woody support passes behind the bird. Bill, red eye, black mask and woven grass are clear.
candidates.fictionBoundary: Missing the branch, catching the rim, earlier dropped grass, alternating foot tests and suppressing the urge to remove a strand are fictional. The image supports suspension beneath the nest and contact with woven material, not a recorded fall or a measurement of the force borne by each foot. The visible wooden support must not be erased from alt text.
candidates.canon: Existing adult male Faye. Preserve Okavango floodplain home (-19.332,23.018), avatar, and every old literal body. This recovers the held first-loop/support premise in a completed-nest scene. It is not an additional duplicate if The loop that stayed is later admitted; the lead must choose one presentation of first trust. No female visit or nest acceptance added. Source Pretoria is provenance, not travel.
candidates.payoff: His tidying reflex becomes a threat to the very structure holding him. He interrupts that reflex with his bill rather than stating a lesson about craftsmanship.
candidates.reviewFlag: Strong detailed exact image. Some individual contact points are obscured by the rim and support; the prose is an invented earlier catch and test, not a claim that the still proves both feet completely independent of wood.

candidates.subject: reticulated glass frog
candidates.title: Past my foot
candidates.body:
For days I had pressed myself against the eggs and kept them wet. I knew the rounded edges beneath my belly. When something moved there, I settled closer.

The first one came free while I was moving across the clutch. A tail where I was used to a round thing. It dropped.

I reached after it with one foot.

It went past. I heard the stream, the same sound it had been making while I guarded them. There was nothing down there for my toes to hold.

Pulled my foot back against the leaf. Sat over the others. One turned beneath me, and I lifted myself to see.

It was still inside its egg. I settled again, a little to one side this time.
candidates.visibleScene: Reticulated glass frog attends a clutch of round translucent eggs attached to the veined underside of a leaf. A second, sparser gelatinous patch lies beside it. The pictured eggs have conspicuous yellow contents. No hatchling is visibly dropping.
candidates.fictionBoundary: Days of attendance, one egg hatching, a reflexive reaching foot, the sound and presence of the stream below and shifting aside are imagined temporal events. Do not identify the sparse patch as definitely hatched or claim the photographed eggs are at an immediately pre-hatching stage. The still anchors the father beside his eggs, not a documentary hatch sequence.
candidates.canon: Existing adult male Moss, current avatar and Caribbean lowland Costa Rica home (10.431,-84.007) unchanged. All current narrative slots are null-media. This is a proposed image-led revision of the held The downward beginning premise, not a second distinct hatch event. Keep that exact old passage privately and do not admit both. Source Puntarenas is provenance, not a move. No offspring count, mate identity, dead tadpole, rescue or lasting injury added.
candidates.payoff: The foot that reflexively follows a departing hatchling has nothing to hold. He returns to the remaining eggs but leaves slightly more room. The changed position carries his conflicted care without a maxim.
candidates.reviewFlag: Clear father-and-clutch relationship, with moderate flash and softer fine detail. Hatching itself is not pictured. Lead must judge whether this before/around-hatching illustration supports the longer imagined sequence; do not claim an exact photographed stage it does not show.

heldStories.subject: satanic leaf-tailed gecko
heldStories.title: Late leaf
heldStories.body:
The wind shook every dead leaf except me.

I swayed to catch up. It stopped.

Held myself at the new angle, waiting for the others to move again.
heldStories.reason: Actual draft evaluated and rejected. Exact camouflage photograph is excellent, but the whole comic mechanism is unseen wind timing. It reads like a general camouflage caption and also risks implying documented species-specific swaying mimicry. No such behavior claim was verified. Preserve only as a held draft.

heldStories.subject: southern masked weaver
heldStories.title: Extra green
heldStories.body:
Pulled a little green strip. The leaves came with it.

It was so much more than I had expected that I kept hold.

Now I'm trying to remember which part of the nest needed a tree.
heldStories.reason: Sharp male with a large green frond, explicitly described as carrying nest material. Prose nevertheless boils down to oversized cargo and a late quip. It adds no distinct consequence and would pad the Story count. No admission proposed.

preservedLegacyPassages.title: The loop that stayed
preservedLegacyPassages.body:
I carried a green strip to the branch and bent it around the fork. Held one end with my foot. Pulled the other with my bill. The whole thing slid free and came with me when I leaned back.

The next strip did the same. The third caught on a rough place in the bark. I tugged it, harder this time, and it held.

I hung beneath it to test the join. My weight drew it tight. The loose end tickled my face, but I left it alone while I dangled there. For the first time that morning, something I had made was holding something I was. Then I sneezed and nearly let go.
preservedLegacyPassages.status: old literal held passage preserved, no binding change

preservedLegacyPassages.title: The downward beginning
preservedLegacyPassages.body:
The tadpoles had become dark, wriggling shapes inside the eggs. I sat nearby while rain ticked against the leaves. One moved, then another. The clear mound began to open.

They slipped free and fell toward the stream. I followed each drop with my eyes until there were too many small movements to follow. The water received them without changing its sound.

Afterward I went across the leaf to the place where the clutch had been. It was suddenly easy to move there. I sat down, then stood, then went to the edge. I had spent so long keeping small bodies on that leaf that watching them leave it felt like failing at the thing I had been doing correctly.
